html:
The Abushiri revolt was a rising of the people of the Tanganyika coast in 1888 and 1889 against the German East Africa Company, named after its leader Abushiri ibn Salim.

When the company took over customs and government of the coastal towns, Arab and Swahili traders and African communities rose together, driving the Germans out of most of the coast except Dar es Salaam and Bagamoyo.

The German government sent an army under Hermann von Wissmann, with African soldiers, which recaptured the towns. Abushiri was betrayed and hanged at Pangani in December 1889. The cost led Germany to take over German East Africa from the company. It was the first of several risings, before Maji Maji, in the Swahili towns.
sum: The Abushiri revolt was a rising of the people of the Tanganyika coast in 1888 and 1889 against the German East Africa Company, named after its leader Abushiri ibn Salim.
